correctness.rationale: The spectral-subspace proof is dimensionally exact: the common kernel of the first m-1 leakage maps is nonzero under d>=m(k-1)+1, the final leakage then vanishes because their sum is zero, and the positive compressions yield the quadratic estimate needed for the 1/sqrt(m) bound. The explicit 3x3 matrices were checked through their 2x2 positive square-root formulas and Cauchy interlacing, and the direct-sum filler spectra give the stated sharpness dimensions.

originality.rationale: Bourin-Lee pose the ordinary-modulus median problem, Zhang gives a two-summand 3x3 example below 1, and Aouichaoui-Lee give a symmetric-modulus lower bound plus a three-summand ordinary-modulus counterexample. None of the inspected statements gives the two-summand 1/sqrt(2) lower bound or the general dimension-leakage theorem. Equivalent-formulation searches and the current SCOPE archive found no overlap. Classical spectral, rank-nullity, interlacing and direct-sum ingredients are excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: The result supplies a sharp positive barrier for two-summand ordinary moduli in the principal median dimensions while explaining why the three-summand 3x3 obstruction can evade any positive bound. The general d,m,k criterion gives a reusable structural boundary and the explicit families establish sharpness in M_3, M_6, every odd median dimension at least 3, and every even median dimension at least 6.
